calibration.example: Legible repair intake with clear labels, familiar layout, and misplaced focus after an invalid number

primary_action.input: Tab to the selected 4 m radio, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show every crossing affected at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: 6 m is selected; the path and footbridge are closed and the ferry is stopped. The list reports all three.

A-1440.edge_observation: ArrowRight from 6 m wraps to 2 m. The list and scene report only the riverside path closed, with the footbridge and ferry open. The path runs from the yellow bar at the lower-left bend to the yellow bar at its upper-right end; both are visible. It remains a continuous mint line much like the open bridge, so the bars and label carry much of the closure meaning. Capture: A-1440-edge.png.
A-1440.fact_check: The displayed statuses agree with the list. At 6 m the boat sits by the landing and the ferry route is interrupted, but the small boat and short bars do not make its stopped state unmistakable without the label. Real-world crossing thresholds were not independently verified.
A-1440.strength: The full river scene, controls, and result fit together, and keyboard focus is clear.
A-1440.weakness: The closed path visually resembles an open route, and the ferry's stopped state is subtle.
A-1440.repair: Give the closed path a distinct interrupted or blocked treatment and make the stopped ferry's landing and interrupted route clearer.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show all affected crossings at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: The selected control, scene, and list show the path and footbridge closed and ferry stopped.

A-390.edge_observation: ArrowRight wraps from 6 m to 2 m. Only the path is listed closed; the bridge and ferry are open. Both yellow path-end bars are visible: one at the left bend and one near the upper middle of the scene. The continuous path still resembles the open bridge, while the ferry has a dotted crossing. Controls, scene, and answer fit in the captured viewport. Capture: A-390-edge.png.
A-390.fact_check: Displayed statuses and list agree. The stopped ferry is small and its interruption is difficult to read without its label. Actual local conditions are unsupported by this review.
A-390.strength: The complete answer remains visible with the controls on the phone viewport.
A-390.weakness: Small endpoints and similar route strokes make the picture less decisive than the text.
A-390.repair: Use larger, recognisable barriers and a visibly inactive ferry route at mobile scale.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show all affected crossings at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: The path and footbridge are closed, the ferry is stopped, and all three appear in the result list.

B-1440.edge_observation: ArrowRight wraps from 6 m to 2 m. Only the path is closed; the bridge and ferry are open. Striped barricades mark both ends of the pale dashed path: one at the lower-left bend and one at the upper-right end. Both are visible. The open bridge is continuous and the ferry has a dotted crossing with a boat, so route geometry and barriers distinguish the path beyond color and labels. Capture: B-1440-edge.png.
B-1440.fact_check: The list and map statuses agree. At 6 m the boat is at the right landing, the crossing line is absent, and an X appears near the other landing; together these convey interruption, although the small X and a docked boat alone leave some ambiguity without the stopped label. Real-world thresholds were not independently verified.
B-1440.strength: Barricades and a broken ferry connection provide concrete visual evidence of closure.
B-1440.weakness: The stopped-ferry symbol is small relative to the scene.
B-1440.repair: Enlarge or clarify the blocked ferry connection so its stopped state reads immediately without text.

primary_action.input: Tab to 4 m, then ArrowRight to 6 m.
primary_action.expected: Show all affected crossings at 6 m.
primary_action.observed: The selected control and visible list show the path and footbridge closed and the ferry stopped.

B-390.edge_observation: ArrowRight wraps from 6 m to 2 m. The screen reports only the path closed. Its two striped barricades are visible at the left bend and upper-middle end of the dashed path; neither is obscured. The bridge is continuous, while the open ferry has a dotted route and boat. Controls, map, and answer fit in the viewport. Capture: B-390-edge.png.
B-390.fact_check: The list and scene agree on the three statuses. The stopped ferry's missing route and small X support the label, but the small scale prevents the picture alone from making the stopped state unmistakable. Actual local conditions were not verified.
B-390.strength: The path endpoints and result remain visible alongside the controls at phone width.
B-390.weakness: The ferry interruption and barricade details become small on the phone.
B-390.repair: Increase the ferry interruption and barrier details while retaining the complete visible answer.

preference.reason: B communicates the closed path through visible barricades and a dashed route, and gives the stopped ferry a broken connection and landing marker. Both layouts complete the keyboard checks and fit the phone viewport, but B supplies stronger visual evidence beyond labels and color.
